title: Samsung creates CEO-led robotics unit to speed commercialization
content: Samsung Electronics has created a robotics business unit reporting directly to its chief executive, bringing strategy, technology development, data collection and factory deployment into a more integrated structure as the company moves humanoid robots closer to commercialization.

title: South Korean president to meet Nvidia and OpenAI CEOs on US trip
content: South Korean president Jae-Myung Lee will launch an economic diplomacy tour centered on AI, advanced industries, and supply chain cooperation, including planned meetings with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and other global tech leaders to discuss AI partnerships. Samsung Electronics, SK Group, Hyundai Motor Group, and Naver executives will also join the trip in force.

title: IBM trims revenue outlook as hardware demand reshapes client spending
content: IBM lowered its full-year revenue growth target after a second-quarter miss, saying clients shifted spending toward scarce hardware and away from software deals. Management framed the weakness as delayed demand rather than lost business, while reaffirming free cash flow growth, margin expansion plans, and confidence in the company's long-term software and mainframe franchises.

title: D-Link robot line starts in 3Q26; care model due in 2027
content: Networking brand D-Link has set up a subsidiary, D-Link Robotics, and is officially entering the service robot market. The new unit will focus on two niche applications, "smart companionship" and "safe care," while adopting an asset-light model built around connectivity, subscription-based management services, SaaS, cloud platforms, and AI ecosystems.

title: Japan loosens fiscal reins for JPY370 trillion AI, semiconductor strategy
content: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's government has approved a sweeping economic strategy that relaxes long-standing fiscal constraints to fund JPY370 trillion (approx. US$2.3 trillion) in public and private investments across artificial intelligence, semiconductors, and other strategic industries through fiscal 2040.

title: Transsion raises phone prices to offset memory-chip inflation and weaker shipments
content: Transsion Holdings, Africa's largest smartphone vendor, expects revenue and profit to rise sharply in the first half of 2026 after higher handset prices offset weaker unit sales and rising memory-chip costs.

title: Sino-American Silicon Products, United Renewable Energy launch US solar module venture
content: Sino-American Silicon Products (SAS) and United Renewable Energy (URECO) announced that they will jointly invest in establishing a solar module manufacturing company in the US, with plans to build a solar module plant with an annual capacity of 1 gigawatt (GW) to meet the surging power demand from artificial intelligence (AI) data centers.

title: Moonshot AI model challenges EDA moat with 2-day chip design
content: China AI startup Moonshot AI has drawn intense attention from the semiconductor industry after unveiling its new large language model Kimi K3, which delivered strong results across multiple model benchmarks and demonstrated an AI agent completing a full chip design flow in 48 hours using open-source electronic design automation (EDA) tools.

title: STMicroelectronics raises AI data center ambition as second-quarter revenue rebounds 26%
content: STMicroelectronics (ST) has raised its revenue ambition for AI data centers to above US$1 billion in 2026 and well above US$2 billion in 2027, staking a larger claim on the AI infrastructure buildout as the European chipmaker swung back to profit in the second quarter of 2026.

title: Tesla confirms equipment orders for TeraFab, targets in-house chip production to break supply bottleneck
content: Tesla has placed equipment orders for an in-house semiconductor development facility in Austin it calls TeraFab, CEO Elon Musk confirmed during the company's Q2 2026 earnings call on July 22, marking a significant step toward chip self-sufficiency.

title: Samsung weighs Besi's Korean rivals for 50-bonder hybrid bonding line as pricing talks drag on
content: Samsung Electronics is preparing a die-to-wafer hybrid bonding production line with about 50 bonders at its Pyeongtaek campus for next-generation high-bandwidth memory and logic chips, according to The Elec.

title: Mitsubishi Electric and Sony Semiconductor Solutions form AI factory automation venture
content: Mitsubishi Electric and Sony Group subsidiary Sony Semiconductor Solutions announced on July 22, 2026, that they have signed a partnership agreement to launch a joint venture focused on using image sensors to automate manufacturing sites and develop physical AI technology. The new company will be 60% funded by Mitsubishi Electric and 40% by Sony.

title: Intel 18A adopts High-NA EUV in dual-certification push
content: Intel Foundry has moved high numerical aperture (High-NA) EUV lithography into production on its Intel 18A process, with ASML confirming in a recent press release that Intel is using the expensive next-generation tool on selected layers of its latest notebook processors, including Panther Lake and the Core Ultra Series 3 built on Intel's 18A technology. The move comes years earlier than Intel's original roadmap, but it currently remains in use for some layers of the 18A process is not replacing

title: Wistron launches first US-made Nvidia GB300 compute baseboard
content: Wistron opened its D1 AI smart factory in Fort Worth, Texas, on July 21 local time, and began mass production of the first Nvidia GB300 compute baseboard made in the US. The nearly US$700 million plant, which spans about 324,000 square feet, was unveiled by Wistron chairman Simon Lin and Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang.

title: Server CPUs are AI boom's next scarce commodity: Intel, AMD reportedly lock in Chinese buyers
content: The AI build-out has found its next pinch point. After spreading from Nvidia's accelerators to memory and networking gear, the scramble for capacity has now reached the once-plentiful server processor, and Chinese cloud and internet firms are being pushed into the kind of long-term supply commitments once reserved for the tightest parts of the market.

title: Tesla names TSMC, Samsung, Micron as key partners for Optimus robot scale-up
content: Tesla is building an entirely new supply chain from scratch to support its Optimus humanoid robot program, with CEO Elon Musk naming TSMC, Samsung, and Micron as critical partners during the company's second quarter 2026 earnings call on July 22, 2026.

title: Texas Instruments sees China EV surge and rising analog prices as upcycle broadens
content: Texas Instruments' second quarter of 2026 results landed Wednesday with two signals worth parsing beyond the headline numbers: an automotive demand acceleration that TI's own management didn't see coming three months ago, and the first analog price increases the company has executed in years. Together, they suggest the current upcycle is broadening in ways the supply chain has not fully absorbed.

An Exynos Chip’s Overheating Saga Would Have Turned Into A Colossal Disaster If One Of Samsung’s Foldable Smartphones Hadn’t Issued A Warning To The Owner
content: In regions outside of the U.S. where only Exynos-powered Galaxy flagships are sold, customers have little choice but to proceed with the purchase, but one Galaxy S22 Ultra owner recounts the time the latter’s overheating problem became so dire that it could have turned into a nightmare. Luckily, the person had another Samsung smartphone, this time, a Galaxy Z Fold 6, to warn him of any impending dangers. Suffice to say that this will be the last time he ever purchases an Exynos-powered handset.
